sections.h2: How can a Ramapo owner sell without the usual delays?
sections.html:
Find out which of Ramapo's overlapping governments bills and permits your house, settle the tax and certificate questions early, and pick a buyer who can close without waiting on a lender. That first step matters here because the town holds a dozen incorporated villages and several hamlets, and each village collects its own taxes.

Ramapo lies in Rockland County, with a land area of 61.14 square miles, New Jersey to the south and Orange County to the west. Mid-2025 brings a Census estimate of 161,564 people, 8.5% above the 2020 base. At the 2020 count no other New York town outside Long Island was larger.

sections.h2: Which communities make up the Town of Ramapo?
sections.html:
Ramapo is a patchwork. Its villages are Airmont, Chestnut Ridge, Hillburn, Kaser, Montebello, New Hempstead, New Square, Pomona, Sloatsburg, Spring Valley, Suffern and Wesley Hills. Monsey, Viola, Hillcrest, Tallman and Sterlington are hamlets, not villages.

The land explains some of it. At Suffern the Ramapo River cuts a gap through the Ramapo Mountains, and the pass carries the Thruway, Interstate 287, State Route 17 and a railroad. State Route 59 runs from Nyack through Spring Valley to Suffern, and the Palisades Interstate Parkway touches the northeast corner. Torne Mountain in Harriman State Park overlooks the pass, and tradition says Washington watched the British fleet from its summit in 1777. The first railroad across Rockland County, built in 1841, ran from Piermont to Ramapo, and Ramapo Iron Works was an early maker of nails and screws. A 1971 case, Golden v. Planning Board of Ramapo, later became a landmark for growth management.

  • Suffern Central School District serves the western part of town.
  • East Ramapo Central School District serves the east, including Spring Valley, Monsey, Pomona, Chestnut Ridge and New Hempstead.
  • Rockland Community College sits in Viola, about four miles east of Suffern.

The district on your parcel decides which school tax bill a buyer inherits, so name it correctly in the listing and on the disclosure form.

sections.h2: How does the Census describe Ramapo homes?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home is valued at $653,100, and the average household has nearly four people. The figures below come from Census Bureau QuickFacts and cover the five survey years ending in 2024 unless a row shows another date.

With 3.84 people per household and nearly four in ten residents under 18, space is in demand, so additions and converted basements are common reasons a certificate of occupancy question comes up. Among residents aged five and older, 59.0% speak a language other than English at home, so listing materials in more than one language can widen your pool of buyers. The building section below covers permits.

sections.h2: Who collects tax in Ramapo, and how does that play out at closing?
sections.html:
The Town of Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, but not for the villages. The town's own FAQ is explicit: each village bills and collects separately, so a house in Airmont or Suffern has a village bill that the town does not handle.

  • County and town tax may be split into four installments for a 5% service charge. The Town gets the first by January 31, and the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance collects installments 2 through 4.
  • School tax cannot be split, because the Receiver does not take partial payments on the school bill.
  • Penalties begin in October for school taxes and in February for county and town taxes.
  • Under Real Property Tax Law section 922, a bill that never arrived does not excuse lateness.

The Receiver's advice to anyone about to sell is to skip the installment plan. It adds 5% of the bill and can muddy the closing, where the seller is credited for the unused part of the taxes. The tax office at (845) 357-5100 can supply a payoff or a tax history, and your attorney should check village bills on their own. Owners who pay off a mortgage are asked to send the satisfaction letter to both the town and village tax offices so later bills reach the right address.

sections.h2: What if a Ramapo tax bill looks wrong or a payment runs late?
sections.html:
An error on a bill goes to the Town of Ramapo Assessor first. The Receiver cannot change a bill alone, and a corrected one is issued only after signed Correction to the Tax Roll paperwork comes back from the Rockland County Real Property Tax Department.

Timing is strict. The town says only an official U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as proof of payment date, and a meter stamp does not. Checks sent through a bank's bill pay often carry no postmark, so a payment must actually arrive by the due date. Credit and debit cards work online only, with a third-party processing fee. Penalties are fixed by state law, and the Receiver has no authority to waive them for any reason.

Before closing, settle these points so a payment does not cross the title date: confirm what has been paid, ask whether any installment remains open, and get the school and county and town figures in writing for your attorney.

sections.h2: What should a Ramapo owner check with the Building Department?
sections.html:
Building, Planning and Zoning reviews permits and supports the Planning Board and the Zoning Board of Appeals. The department says it wants the permit and certificate of occupancy process to be as simple as possible, and its page lists forms that matter for unusual properties.

  • A list of required inspections for one- and two-family dwellings, which shows the steps a permitted project must pass.
  • A Certificate of Use application.
  • A Secondary Dwelling application, for a second unit on the property.
  • A Plumbing Test Certification form.

An online Property Search tool is also available. Use it with the permit application package to compare the town's file against what stands on the lot. After a basement conversion, a new kitchen or an addition, confirm a certificate of occupancy exists, because buyers' attorneys ask and New York's disclosure form puts the same question to the seller.

sections.h2: What does a Ramapo seller owe to transfer the deed?
sections.html:
The Rockland County Clerk receives the deed along with the TP-584 transfer tax return and the RP-5217 transfer report. The county sets recording fees, so ask the clerk for the current amounts, and ask your attorney when the TP-584 must be filed.

The state transfer tax is two dollars per $500 of price, rounded upward, and the seller usually pays it. Take a $653,100 sale: it is taxed as $653,500, which is 1,307 units of $500, for a tax of $2,614. A buyer of a residence at a million dollars or more pays a further 1% mansion tax.

The disclosure form carries its own duty. A seller of a house with up to four dwelling units signs it and delivers it ahead of a binding contract. If you later learn something that makes the form inaccurate, a revised copy is due as soon as practicable, though never after title transfers or the buyer moves in, whichever comes first.

faqs.q: Will the Town of Ramapo's tax office bill my village taxes?
faqs.a: No. The town's FAQ says each village bills and collects separately, so a house inside a village has a village bill on top of the town, county and school bills.

faqs.q: Is Ramapo's installment plan a good idea before a sale?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver of Taxes advises against it, since it adds a 5% charge and can cause problems at closing.

faqs.q: How do I tell which school district my Ramapo house belongs to?
faqs.a: The west, including Suffern, Montebello, Airmont, Sloatsburg and Hillburn, is mainly Suffern Central, and the east is East Ramapo Central, so confirm against your school tax bill.

faqs.q: How is the state transfer tax figured on a Ramapo sale?
faqs.a: Two dollars per $500 of price, rounded up. A $653,100 sale rounds to $653,500 and owes $2,614.

faqs.q: How do I learn whether my Ramapo house has a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: Try the town's Property Search tool first, then confirm with the Building Department by phone at (845) 357-5100.
